sources: dossier=api-key dossier Rotation bullet (partial unique index lets two rows share a name, silent on expiry); doc=api-key.md Name-uniqueness invariant (pre-edit called it the "active-name uniqueness index"); code=postgres/sqlite 001-initial.sql migrations, rimsky_api_keys_active_name_idx WHERE revoked_at IS NULL AND revoke_at IS NULL (no expires_at term)
note: The doc's own Active-status predicate (one bullet above) includes expiry, so naming this the "active-name" index implied expired-but-unrevoked rows free their name; the index predicate only excludes revoked/grace-scheduled rows. Reworded to state the actual exclusion and note an expired-but-unrevoked row still blocks reuse.

sources: dossier=api-key dossier Rotation required-behavior bullet ("mints a new key with the same name/permissions/expires_at"); doc=api-key.md Rotate lifecycle bullet (pre-edit named only name + permissions); code=auth_handlers.go Rotate handler copies ExpiresAt from the old row to the new row
note: Dossier and code agree expiry carries across rotation; the doc's Rotate bullet omitted it. Added expiry to the list of what a rotation copies forward.

sources: dossier=dry-run dossier (floor is grant-mode-vs-flag, silent on multi-entry resolution) and permission dossier (set-membership evaluation, no first-match-wins); doc=dry-run.md floor paragraph (pre-edit); code=lib/foundation/auth/check.go CheckGrant (execute promoted over dry_run across matches), lib/control/controlapi/auth_middleware.go (same reduction); test=auth_middleware_test.go::TestGate_ExecuteBeatsDryRun_MultiEntryGrant, check_mode_scope_test.go pinning execute-beats-dry-run regardless of order
note: A dedicated named test plus the matching production code corroborate that an execute-mode entry lifts the floor when it coexists with a matching dry-run entry; the doc's floor paragraph didn't say this and could be read as "any matching dry-run entry pins the key." Added the cross-entry resolution rule.

sources: doc=dry-run.md "What it is" section, paragraph 1 closing sentence and paragraph 2 opening sentence (near-verbatim restatement of the EITHER-flag-OR-grant-mode resolution)
note: Purely a self-evident prose-tightness defect (redundant restatement), not an intent dispute — verified directly against the doc's own text. Folded into the same edit as row 267: removed the redundant preamble and kept only the floor/new-content clause.

sources: dossier=message-schema dossier (silent on invariant numbering, no conflict); doc=message-schema.md body-inertness bullet (pre-edit cited invariant: 21); corpus=concepts/inertness.md invariant registry (§21 = blob content + executor error payloads; §24 = message payloads, explicitly "read only at the substitution leaf ... and at the persistence-layer fetch")
note: inertness.md is the authoritative invariant registry and assigns message-payload inertness to §24, not §21 (blob/executor-error). Fixed the cross-reference.

sources: same as row 153 finding at 308: dossier=message-schema dossier (silent); doc=message-schema.md body-inertness bullet; corpus=concepts/inertness.md invariant registry (§24 = message payloads)
note: Duplicate of the row-308 finding (same file, same line, same wrong citation). Already fixed by that edit — invariant: 21 corrected to invariant: 24; no separate edit needed.

sources: dossier=permission dossier + dry-run dossier (both describe the resolved mode as floor(grant mode, flag)); doc=permission.md Boundaries (pre-edit Adjacent gloss "orthogonal — the request flag, not a grant property"); corpus=permission.md's own preceding "Does NOT own" clause (dry-run owns resolving the mode; permission owns the grant mode field feeding the floor) and dry-run.md's resolution definition (mode resolves from EITHER the flag OR the identity-bound grant mode)
note: The Adjacent gloss contradicted the immediately preceding sentence in the same Boundaries paragraph and dry-run.md's own definition, both of which treat the grant mode as a real input to dry-run resolution. Reworded the gloss to match.

sources: dossier=api-key/permission dossiers (silent on JSONB specifically, do not claim a postgres-only encoding); doc=permission.md Purpose paragraph (pre-edit "entries are JSONB"); code=postgres/001-initial.sql:43 permissions JSONB NOT NULL vs sqlite/001-initial.sql:56 permissions TEXT NOT NULL, lib/foundation/persistence/api_keys.go Permissions json.RawMessage, backend store read/write paths (both carry JSON-encoded bytes, only the column type differs)
note: Both backends carry JSON content, but only postgres's column type is JSONB; sqlite's is TEXT. Genericized the wording to backend-neutral "JSON" so the claim holds under both backends; the load-bearing fact (forward-compatible parser preserving unknown fields) is unaffected.

sources: dossier=write-semantics dossier (ModeCoexists takes one shared value by design; byte-equal-scope uniformity documented separately); doc=write-semantics.md Per-value-semantics paragraph (pre-edit); corpus=concepts/claim-scope.md (uniformity invariant scoped explicitly to byte-equal conflicts; scopes-conflict capability is producer-owned overlap semantics with no rimsky-side uniformity guarantee); code=lib/runtime/runner_acquire_claims.go evaluateClaimScopeConflict (ModeCoexists called with only the holder's RealizedWriteSemantics when scopesConflict reports an overlap on non-byte-equal scope)
note: The doc's justification ("holder and candidate share the producer's realization") holds only for byte-equal-scope conflicts, where claim-scope.md's uniformity invariant guarantees it; for scopes-conflict-capable overlap conflicts the candidate has no realization yet and only the holder's is used. Reworded to distinguish the two cases; the single-shared-value claim itself (and the enum/gate design) is unaffected.

sources: dossier=write-semantics dossier ("the atomic-staging reference producer ... Open reserves a private staging area returned with realized staged_async ... the atomicity lives in the producer, not rimsky"); doc=write-semantics.md Boundaries Adjacent list (pre-edit omitted atomic-staging); corpus=concepts/atomic-staging.md Definition (producer-side stage-then-swap pattern realizing the same staged_async value)
note: The dossier and atomic-staging.md both tie the staged-asynchronous realized value directly to atomic-staging's stage-then-swap discipline; the omission from write-semantics' own Adjacent list was a real gap. Added atomic-staging to the Adjacent list. The reverse omission (atomic-staging.md not listing write-semantics) is out of scope — that file is not one of this pass's five judged concept docs.
